correctness.rationale: For each given fixed path, the published tree-inclusion theorem supplies its exact probability; path enumeration is disjoint and the mass telescopes to the stated upper-tail product. The cross-parameter factor-difference is exact with a positive denominator and strictly decreasing bracket in the tail index. It proves the stochastic trichotomy including boundary support, the equal-support exceptional pair, at most one tail sign crossing, the first incomparable N=11, and the asymptotic x=2/3 sign boundary. The proof treats quantifiers, labels, support endpoints and normalization. Standalone exact verifier passed 89,613 assertions; finite checking corroborates but is not relied on for the infinite statements.

value.rationale: For the natural probability statistic of distance between two marked same-part vertices of a fixed-order bipartite uniform spanning tree, complete comparison across graph imbalance is structurally nontrivial: reversing effects, a sharp finite incomparability obstruction and a single-crossing property resolve the global order relation, while the 2/3 macroscopic boundary organizes the whole family.
